newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal budget restrains spending - minister.
newsitem.headline: Portugal budget restrains spending - minister.

text.p: Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco said on Wednesday that the 1997 budget plan would give Portugal, for the first time, a surplus of current revenues over current spending.

Defending the plan in parliament at the start of a two-day debate, Sousa Franco said the budget called for a current surplus, excluding debt financing and investment, of 147.8 billion escudos against a deficit of 62 billion in 1996.
"The 1997 implies strong restraint on spending, stronger restraint than that achieved in 1996," he said.
Sousa Franco said the budget plan, which forecasts a deficit of 2.9 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) for next year, would achieve its aims without any increase in taxes.
The budget is crucial to Portugal's campaign to win a place in the European Union's planned Economic and Monetary Union in 1999.
Sousa Franco said that government current spending would rise only 4.6 percent compared with 1996.
He reaffirmed his confidence that economic growth could reach the government's 2.75 percent target this year.
